details: CONFIRMED (reproduced). The SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers in relay_ci.main() and the finally around the steps only run when
bin/ci itself is signalled softly. Under relay gate, the only place a probe exists, a stopped gate SIGKILLs the whole
process group (lib/relay_gate.py, master and wt/gate-lock alike), so relay_ci's finally never runs. With the bash gate
the same leak happened only when the stop came during the probe (the last ~half of a gate); with B the probe exists
from the first second, so every stopped gate leaks one detached worktree plus a full checkout in TMPDIR. Stopping a gate
is ordinary use (Ctrl-C, a session that ends, the front stopping a wrong run). The tests cover only an in-process
KeyboardInterrupt, not the real stop path.
evidence: python3 scratchpad/rep/stopgate.py <worktree> <dir>   (script: Popen bin/ci --quick with start_new_session, killpg SIGKILL)
Live: git -C /Users/amidman/relay worktree list on 26 Oct shows 9 detached probe worktrees under
/var/folders/.../T/tmp.XXXXXXXXXX/wt (bash mktemp names, from the bash gate): the leak already accumulates when a stop
hits the probe phase; B widens it to the whole gate. (Some may be probes of gates running now; not separated.)
failing_case: A temp repo with the branch's bin/ci and lib/relay_ci.py, tests/run_unittest.py sleeping 30 s; run what relay gate
runs: Popen(["bin/ci","--quick"], env RELAY_GATE=<head>, start_new_session=True); after 3 s os.killpg(pid, SIGKILL)
(what lib/relay_gate.py does in its finally when the gate gets SIGTERM, SIGHUP or Ctrl-C).
Now: `git worktree list` still shows /var/folders/.../T/tmp7c5b4qpj/wt (detached) and the full checkout stays on disk;
the next gate in that worktree does not remove it. Should: no probe worktree left once the gate is stopped, or at the
latest the next gate of that worktree removes the leftover one (design case 3: "the probe is stopped and its worktree
fix_hint: Inside this change: Probe.start() writes the probe's temp path to the outer `.ci/inert-probe` before `git worktree add`;
at the start of every run (prepare) a recorded path that is still there is removed (`git worktree remove --force`,
prune, rmtree) and the record deleted; stop() deletes the record. The per-worktree gate lock (wt/gate-lock) makes this
safe against a second gate of the same worktree. Optional, outside (lib/relay_gate.py, the other branch): SIGTERM the
group, a short grace, then SIGKILL.
pass_cases: 1. The reproduction above, then a second `RELAY_GATE=<head> bin/ci --quick` run in the same worktree to its end:
`git worktree list` lists only the main checkout, and the leftover temp folder is gone.
2. Two worktrees of one repo gating at once: the cleanup in one never removes the other's live probe worktree
(only the probe recorded for this worktree is removed).
3. tests/test_ci_python.py::ProbeBesideTheRun (stop, KeyboardInterrupt in a step, killed probe) still pass.
4. A gate that runs to its end leaves no probe worktree and no record of one (as today).
reason: tests/test_ci_python.py:278 (fails at base, passes now), :295, :308 pass; record written before worktree, removed on stop, leftover removed in prepare.
findings.summary: a stopped relay gate (killpg SIGKILL) leaves the probe's worktree registered and its checkout in TMPDIR, now at any point of the gate

details: PLAUSIBLE (traced; not reproduced, gate-lock is not in master). Narrow: relay gate itself kills the whole group, so this
needs the gate program alone to die. Size: 15 agent minutes (close_fds=False, or pass_fds of the inherited lock fd
evidence: git diff master...wt/gate-lock -- lib/relay_gate.py: Popen(..., start_new_session=True, pass_fds=(lock.fileno(),))
lib/relay_ci.py:138 subprocess.Popen(list(self.nested), ...) and :216 self.runner(argv, **kwargs): close_fds default True
failing_case: With wt/gate-lock landed: relay gate passes its lock file to bin/ci (pass_fds) so the lock lives until the command's
last process ends. bash passed that fd to every child; Python's subprocess closes it (close_fds=True default) in the
probe (Popen at :138) and every step (Ci.run). If the bin/ci python process alone is killed (kill -9 <pid>, OOM) while
its library tests or probe run on, the lock is freed and a second gate of the same worktree can start beside the
orphans. Should: the lock held until the last process of the command ends, as the design promises (F4 of its review).
fix_hint: Pass close_fds=False to the Popen of the probe and to Ci.run's subprocess calls (the gate opens no other fds a child
must not have), or keep it and let the lock fd through by number.
pass_cases: 1. bin/ci started with an inherited flock fd; kill -9 of the bin/ci python while a step's child sleeps: a non-blocking
flock on the same file still fails until that child ends.
2. A gate that runs to its end frees the lock when it ends (as today).
reason: tests/test_ci_python.py:323 fails at base (AssertionError 1 != 0), passes now; close_fds=False at relay_ci.py:165 and :240.
findings.summary: children of the Python gate no longer inherit the worktree lock fd that wt/gate-lock passes to the command
